subtitle: An arrow in the dust that decided an empire

panels.shot: epic split composition, half showing Hemu on a war elephant, half showing young Akbar under a battle standard
panels.action: Hemu, fierce and resolute atop a towering war elephant, faces a distant, composed young Akbar beside Bairam Khan on a ridge, the hazy plain of Panipat between them under a harsh November sun.

dialogue.text: On a dusty field near Panipat, one arrow felled a usurper, restored a dynasty, and left a question history still cannot answer: who truly struck Hemu down?

i18n.hi: पानीपत के सूखे मैदान पर, एक तीर ने गद्दार गिराया, सल्तनत लौटा दी, और छोड़ गया सवाल: हेमू को सच में किसने ढेर किया?

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of North India, with overlapping vignettes
panels.action: A sweeping vista of North India shows Delhi’s domes under Hemu’s banners in one corner, and in another, young Akbar and Bairam Khan riding through rugged country with a small, disciplined Mughal force.

dialogue.text: In 1556, Delhi had already slipped from the Mughals’ hands. Hemu, the brilliant general of the Surs, now called himself Vikramaditya and sat on the throne Humayun had just reclaimed and lost forever.

i18n.hi: १५५६ तक, दिल्ली मुगलों के हाथ से फिसल चुकी थी। सूरों का तेजस General हेमू अब विक्रमादित्य कहलाता था, और हुमायूँ की छिनी हुई गद्दी पर बेखौफ बैठा था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Hemu in court
panels.action: Inside a Delhi hall, Hemu sits confident on a richly carved throne, armour beneath his robes, courtiers around him as he studies maps of North India spread on a low table.

dialogue.text: Born a trader’s son from Rewari, hardened in Sher Shah’s wars, Hemu rose as a soldier and commander. With Humayun dead and the Surs divided, he seized Delhi and dreamed of ruling from Kabul to the sea.

i18n.hi: रेवाड़ी के बनिये का बेटा, शेरशाह की जंगों में सख्त हुआ, हेमू सिपाही से सरदार बना। हुमायूँ मर चुका था, सूर बिखरे थे, तो उसने दिल्ली छीनी और काबुल से समंदर तक राज का सपना देखा।

panels.shot: medium shot of Bairam Khan briefing Akbar in a tent
panels.action: In a wind-flapped campaign tent, Bairam Khan, stern and authoritative, leans over a young Akbar seated on a simple cushion, pointing to a rough map while officers listen in tense silence.

dialogue.text: Far to the northwest, a boy-king marched. Akbar, barely fourteen, rode under the guidance of his regent, Bairam Khan. To keep Kabul, they had to reclaim Delhi; to reclaim Delhi, they had to break Hemu.

i18n.hi: उधर उत्तर-पश्चिम में एक बाल-सम्राट बढ़ता आया। अकबर, बस चौदह बरस का, अपने उस्ताद बैरम ख़ाँ के साथ घोड़े पर सवार। काबुल बचाना था तो दिल्ली लेनी थी, और दिल्ली के लिए हेमू को तोड़ना था।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of both armies approaching Panipat from opposite sides
panels.action: From one side, Hemu’s massive host advances, elephants in the lead and banners fluttering; from the other, the more compact Mughal army moves in ordered lines toward the flat expanse of Panipat.

dialogue.text: Panipat had seen empires born before. Now, once again, two claimants to Hindustan chose this flat, open plain to settle the question with cavalry, cannon, and elephants.

i18n.hi: पानीपत पहले भी साम्राज्य जगा चुका था। अब फिर, हिंदुस्तान के दो दावेदारों ने यही समतल मैदान चुना—यहाँ घुड़सवार, तोपें और हाथी फैसला करेंगे।

panels.shot: close shot of Hemu on his elephant preparing for battle
panels.action: Hemu stands tall in full armour atop a huge war elephant, hand resting on his sword hilt as he looks over his army, the animal’s forehead plated in metal and bells glinting in the morning light.

dialogue.speaker: Hemu
dialogue.text: Forward! Today we drive the Mughals back to Kabul!

i18n.hi: आगे बढ़ो! आज मुगलों को काबुल तक धकेल देंगे!

panels.shot: medium shot of Akbar mounted, with Bairam Khan beside him
panels.action: Akbar sits on a horse in light mail, his face young but set, while Bairam Khan rides alongside, gesturing toward the enemy lines and the Mughal artillery positioned between them.

dialogue.speaker: Bairam Khan
dialogue.text: Stay behind the guns, Padshah. Let our cannon speak first.

i18n.hi: तोपों के पीछे रहिए, बादशाह। पहले हमारी घाटियाँ बोलें।

panels.shot: dynamic battle-wide shot showing initial clash
panels.action: On the open plain, Mughal cannon belch smoke while Hemu’s war elephants, tusks sheathed in armor, lumber forward through exploding dust, cavalry swirling around them in chaotic, desperate motion.

dialogue.text: The first volleys shook the earth. Yet, as Abul Fazl and later scholars agree, Hemu’s elephant charge crashed through the Mughal centre and for a moment their line wavered on the edge of flight.

i18n.hi: पहली तोपों की गूँज से ज़मीन काँप उठी। फिर भी, अबुल फ़ज़ल और बाद के कई इतिहासकार मानते हैं कि हेमू के हाथी-दल ने मुगल बीचोंबीच चीर डाला, और एक पल को उनकी صف लड़खड़ा उठी।

panels.shot: tight, chaotic mid-shot focusing on Mughal cavalry in disarray
panels.action: Mughal horsemen reel back, some turning their mounts away from the oncoming elephants, dust swirling around them as standard-bearers struggle to keep their banners aloft.

dialogue.text: Chroniclers speak of confusion in the Mughal ranks. For soldiers who remembered Humayun’s defeats and Sur strength, the sight of Hemu’s elephants tearing into their centre must have felt like history repeating.

i18n.hi: इतिहासकार मुगल फ़ौज में घबराहट लिखते हैं। जिन सिपाहियों ने हुमायूँ की हारें और सूरों की ताकत देखी थी, उनके लिए हेमू के हाथी बीच में घुसते ही पुराना डर फिर लौट आया होगा।

panels.shot: sudden close-up on Hemu at the moment the arrow strikes
panels.action: An extreme close-up freezes Hemu at the height of the charge, eyes fixed ahead, as an arrow hurtles toward his face and in the next instant is lodged in his right eye, his body stiffening.

dialogue.text: Then came the arrow. All accounts agree on this: as he urged his elephant deeper into the fray, a shaft struck Hemu in the eye. In an instant, the driving will behind his army vanished.

i18n.hi: फिर आया वो तीर। सारी रिवायतें एक पर मिलती हैं: जैसे ही हेमू अपने हाथी को गहराई तक हाँक रहा था, एक बाण आकर उसकी आँख में धँस गया। पल भर में उसकी सेना की धड़कती जान बुझ गई।

panels.shot: medium shot of Hemu collapsing on his elephant as mahout struggles
panels.action: Hemu collapses unconscious against the wooden howdah, the arrow still in his eye, while his terrified mahout tugs at the goad, the great elephant slowing and turning away from the Mughal line.

dialogue.text: Blinded and fainting, he slumped in the howdah. His mahout wheeled the beast away. On the field below, men who had fought to his voice and his presence suddenly saw only a leaderless elephant retreating into dust.

i18n.hi: अंधा सा होकर, बेहोशी में, वह हौदे में ढह पड़ा। महावत ने हाथी मोड़ा और भाग खड़ा हुआ। नीचे मैदान में, जो सिपाही उसकी आवाज़ और सूरत पर लड़ते थे, उन्होंने बस अपना सरदारहीन हाथी धूल में गुम होता देखा।

panels.shot: wide shot showing the breaking of Hemu’s army
panels.action: Across the battlefield, Hemu’s infantry and cavalry begin to scatter, some dropping weapons, others spurring horses in different directions, while Mughal horsemen press forward in more confident lines.

dialogue.text: Satish Chandra and Jadunath Sarkar note the same turning: once Hemu’s elephant disappeared from the front, the cohesion of his host shattered. Without his command, the Sur army dissolved under renewed Mughal attack.

i18n.hi: सतीश चंद्र और जदुनाथ सरकार भी वही मोड़ लिखते हैं: जैसे ही हेमू का हाथी मोर्चे से ओझल हुआ, उसकी फ़ौज की गिरफ़्त टूट गई। उसके हुक्म के बिन सूर सेना दोबारा मुगल चोट सह न सकी और बिखर गई।

panels.shot: medium shot of Hemu captured and bound, still unconscious
panels.action: Near a grove outside the field, Mughal soldiers stand around Hemu, who lies bound and unconscious on the ground, armour dented, the arrow still lodged, as an officer gestures toward the distant Mughal camp.

dialogue.text: Hemu did not die on the field. Found on his elephant, senseless but alive, he was captured and brought before the young emperor and his regent. Here the smoke of battle lifts; the fog of sources begins.

i18n.hi: हेमू मैदान में नहीं मरा। हाथी पर बेहोश लेकिन ज़िंदा मिला, उसे पकड़ा गया और नौजवान बादशाह व उसके वज़ीर के सामने लाया गया। यहाँ से बारूद का धुआँ हटता है, और स्रोतों की धुंध शुरू।

panels.shot: intimate tent interior, Hemu kneeling, Akbar and Bairam Khan standing
panels.action: Inside a Mughal command tent, Hemu, bleeding from the eye and barely conscious, is propped on his knees, while Akbar stands to one side, expression conflicted, and Bairam Khan looms, hand resting on his sword.

dialogue.text: Abul Fazl, writing for Akbar, tells one story: that the boy-king, urged by his men, struck the fallen Hemu and so earned the title ghazi, warrior of the faith.

i18n.hi: अकबर के लिए लिखने वाले अबुल फ़ज़ल की कहानी और है: कहता है, सिपाही दबाव डालते रहे, तो बाल-अकबर ने गिरे हुए हेमू पर वार किया और घाज़ी, धर्मयोद्धा का खिताब लिया।

panels.shot: closer focus on Akbar’s face, with Bairam Khan’s shadow looming
panels.action: A close shot captures Akbar’s young face in thought, eyes downcast toward Hemu, while behind him Bairam Khan’s profile is dark, his gaze hard and unyielding in the lamplight.

dialogue.text: Yet Badayuni, a sharper, often critical voice at court, records another: that Akbar refused to strike an unconscious man, and that Bairam Khan himself killed Hemu instead.

i18n.hi: पर बदायूँनी, जो दरबार में तेज और अक्सर आलोचक ज़ुबान था, दूसरा किस्सा कहता है: अकबर ने बेहोश आदमी पर हाथ उठाने से इंकार किया, और हेमू को खुद बैरम ख़ाँ ने मार गिराया।

panels.shot: symbolic split-panel style shot evoking the two contradictory versions
panels.action: The scene visually splits: on one side, Akbar is shown raising a sword over Hemu; on the other, the same pose is held by Bairam Khan while Akbar turns away, both images ghostlike, their details indistinct.

dialogue.text: Modern historians read these accounts not as simple fact, but as mirrors of their authors. One burnishes a sovereign’s glory; the other hints at a conscience and shifts the burden onto the regent.

i18n.hi: आज के इतिहासकार इन हवाले को सीधा सच नहीं, बल्कि अपने-अपने लेखक का आईना मानते हैं। एक बादशाह की शान चमकाता है, दूसरा उसके ज़मीर की झलक देता है और दोष वज़ीर पर डालता है।

panels.shot: wide aftermath shot of Panipat field littered with abandoned equipment
panels.action: The battlefield lies quiet at dusk, abandoned shields, spears, and broken gun carriages scattered across the plain, a few scavengers moving among the remnants as distant Mughal standards flutter over a camp.

dialogue.text: Whatever the final stroke, Hemu’s defeat was complete. With his fall at Panipat, the last great attempt to keep the Mughals from the heart of Hindustan collapsed, and Delhi once more opened its gates to a Timurid ruler.

i18n.hi: अंतिम वार चाहे जैसा भी हो, हेमू की हार पूरी थी। पानीपत में उसके गिरते ही मुगलों को रोकने की आख़िरी बड़ी कोशिश ढह गई, और दिल्ली ने फिर एक तैमूरी शहंशाह के लिए फाटक खोल दिए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Akbar in later years, reflective, looking toward Delhi
panels.action: An older Akbar, robed and composed, stands on a high terrace of the Agra fort at sunrise, gazing toward the faint outline of Delhi on the horizon, while attendants wait respectfully behind him.

dialogue.text: From this victory flowed a reign of nearly fifty years, the shaping of an empire that would dominate the subcontinent. Yet at its root lay a teenage battle, a wounded rival, and a contested act that the record never fully clears.

i18n.hi: यही फ़तह आगे चलकर पचास साल की हुकूमत बनी, वो साम्राज्य गढ़ा जिसने पूरे उपमहाद्वीप पर छाया डाली। पर इसकी जड़ में था एक किशोर बादशाह, एक घायल दुश्मन, और एक विवादित वार जिसे इतिहास कभी साफ़ नहीं कर पाया।

panels.shot: final contemplative shot blending Hemu’s and Akbar’s silhouettes over the plain of Panipat
panels.action: In a poetic composition, the silhouettes of Hemu on his elephant and young Akbar on horseback both loom faintly over the empty plain of Panipat, the land itself stretching quiet and indifferent beneath them.

dialogue.text: Second Panipat reminds us that an empire can turn on a single arrow, a single decision, and that even at such turning points, history often leaves us not certainties, but sharp, enduring questions.

i18n.hi: द्वितीय पानीपत याद दिलाता है कि कभी-कभी पूरा साम्राज्य एक तीर, एक फ़ैसले पर मुड़ जाता है—और ऐसे मोड़ों पर भी इतिहास हमें यक़ीन नहीं, बस चुभते, टिके हुए सवाल देकर जाता है।

title_i18n.hi: द्वितीय पानीपत और हेमू का तीर

subtitle_i18n.en: An arrow in the dust that decided an empire
subtitle_i18n.hi: धूल में वो तीर जिसने साम्राज्य पलट दिया
